name: Felix Sater

summary.text: Felix Sater is a Russian-born American businessman. On December 10, 1998 he pleaded guilty in the Eastern District of New York (United States v. Sater, No. 98-cr-1101) to a racketeering count in a $40 million stock-manipulation scheme and became a government cooperator; he was sentenced on October 23, 2009 to probation and a $25,000 fine, and the case was partly unsealed in 2013. He was a principal of Bayrock Group, co-developer of Trump SoHo. In 2010 he carried Trump Organization business cards describing him as a senior adviser to Donald Trump. In 2015-16 he worked with Michael Cohen on a proposed Trump Tower Moscow, for which Trump signed a letter of intent by November 2015, as recorded in the Mueller report and the Senate Intelligence Committee's Volume 5.

facts.claim: On December 10, 1998 Felix Sater pleaded guilty in the Eastern District of New York to one racketeering count in a $40 million stock-manipulation scheme and signed a cooperation agreement; the agreement noted exposure of up to 20 years in prison and up to $60 million in restitution.
facts.quote: the agreement noted up to 20 years in prison, at least $250,000 in fines, and up to $60 million in restitution

facts.claim: The case United States v. Sater, 1:98-cr-01101, was assigned to Judge I. Leo Glasser, filed December 3, 1998 and terminated October 26, 2009; Sater was sentenced on October 23, 2009 to probation and a $25,000 fine after a period of cooperation with the federal government.
facts.quote: Defendant Sater was sentenced on October 23, 2009, after a period of cooperation with the federal government.

sources.title: Estate of Gottdiener v. Sater, 35 F. Supp. 3d 386 (S.D.N.Y. 2014)
United States v. Sater, 1:98-cr-01101

facts.claim: Sater's cooperation had been sealed under the name 'John Doe'; after the clerk's office inadvertently unsealed the docket sheet, the Second Circuit affirmed Judge Glasser's unsealing orders and on March 12, 2013 Glasser unsealed a substantial number of documents in the criminal case.
facts.quote: on March 12, 2013, Judge Glasser unsealed a substantial number of documents in the criminal case against Defendant Sater

facts.claim: Trump's lawyer has said Trump was not aware of Sater's criminal past until at least 2007; in a December 2007 deposition Trump said Bayrock had represented Sater to him as an employee rather than a principal.
facts.quote: Well, they represented to me that he [Sater] was not a principal--[that] he's an employee.

sources.title: Donald Trump And The Felon: Inside His Business Dealings With A Mob-Connected Hustler

facts.claim: An AP investigation found that in 2010 Sater handed out business cards describing himself as a senior adviser to Donald Trump and had an office on the same floor as Trump's in Trump Tower; Trump Organization lawyer Alan Garten said Sater's role was to prospect for high-end real-estate deals and that the arrangement lasted six months.
facts.quote: Sater presented business cards describing himself as a senior adviser to Donald Trump, and he had an office on the same floor as Trump's own office in New York's Trump Tower.

facts.claim: Asked about Sater by the AP, Trump said: 'Felix Sater, boy, I have to even think about it... I'm not that familiar with him.' In a November 2013 deposition he said that if Sater were in the room he would not know what he looked like and that he had conversed with him 'Not many' times.
facts.quote: "Felix Sater, boy, I have to even think about it," Trump said, referring questions about Sater to his staff. "I'm not that familiar with him."

facts.claim: The Mueller report records that candidate Trump signed a letter of intent for Trump Tower Moscow by November 2015 and that in January 2016 Trump Organization executive Michael Cohen emailed and spoke about the project with the office of Kremlin press secretary Dmitry Peskov; the Organization kept pursuing the deal into mid-2016.
facts.quote: Candidate Trump signed a Letter of Intent for Trump Tower Moscow by November 2015, and in January 2016 Trump Organization executive Michael Cohen emailed and spoke about the project with the office of Russian government press secretary Dmitry Peskov.

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice (Special Counsel's Office)
sources.title: Report on the Investigation into Russian Interference in the 2016 Presidential Election, Volume I

facts.claim: BuzzFeed News reported that Sater sent Cohen a 17-page letter of intent on October 13, 2015 describing a development with 250 condos, a hotel and a spa and a $4 million up-front licensing fee, and that in an October 2015 email Sater wrote 'I will get Putin on this program and we will get Donald elected'; in January 2016 Sater suggested Cohen email Peskov because Russian government approvals were needed.
facts.quote: the 17-page letter of intent was sent from Felix Sater to Michael Cohen on Oct. 13, 2015

facts.claim: The November 2018 criminal information against Michael Cohen in the Southern District of New York alleged that his August 2017 letter to the Senate and House intelligence committees falsely described the Moscow project as abandoned, in order to minimize links between the project and Trump and suggest it ended before the Iowa caucus.
facts.quote: The filing alleges those statements were false, made to minimize links between the project and Trump and to suggest the project ended before the Iowa caucus.

facts.claim: The Senate Intelligence Committee's Volume 5 (August 18, 2020) found that during the 2016 cycle Trump Organization leaders received at least three proposals for a Trump Tower in Moscow, two of them made to Michael Cohen by Sater and by Giorgi Rtskhiladze, and that documents Cohen produced suggested Donald Trump Jr. and Sater could have known Cohen's congressional statement falsely represented material facts about the negotiations.
facts.quote: could have known that Cohen's statement falsely represented material facts about negotiations over a deal for a Trump Tower Moscow

facts.claim: Sater testified before the House Intelligence Committee in December 2017; he was interviewed privately by committee staff later in 2019 after missing a June 21, 2019 appearance that his lawyer attributed to health reasons, and the committee said he had not produced subpoenaed documents including unredacted phone records.
facts.quote: Sater said afterward that he spoke truthfully, but the committee issued a rare statement saying he still had not produced documents he was subpoenaed for, including unredacted phone records.

openQuestions: The 2009 '5K1' letter describing Sater's cooperation and the 2019 unsealed documents were only seen via secondary reporting; the filings on the E.D.N.Y. docket should be read directly.
The Mueller report pages on Sater by name were not reached; the Sater email quotations rest on BuzzFeed News and CBS reporting of the emails.
The House Intelligence Committee transcript of Sater's 2019 interview was not located.
